title: One thread runs one command at a time, so each command is atomic
caption: Commands from all clients queue up and run start to finish on a single event loop against data in RAM; disk is a background copy.

steps.text: Two app servers send INCR hits at the same moment.
The loop takes one command, runs it to completion (read 7, write 8, reply 8), then the next (8 → 9). No interleaving, so no lost update.
Persistence happens off the request path: appending to a log (AOF) or forking a snapshot (RDB).
The flip side: a slow command (KEYS *, a huge HGETALL) blocks every client for its whole run time.
